content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a brand new [product_name]. Using a Kingston SD card (FAT32, 16GB). After powering off the [product_name], I inserted the SD card and powered it on, but there was no response on the display until I removed the SD card tray. Even while powered, the SD card isn't recognized when sliding the card tray. Is it possible to get an RMA or return through [company_name]? Thanks in advance. [user_name]

Did you purchase the [product_name] directly from [company_name] or through a dealer? If through a dealer, you should address them for complaints. The card slot for the microSD card is unfortunately fragile and doesn't handle rough handling well. Bent pins in the card slot are a frequent issue; improper or forceful insertion can bend them, causing connection problems.
I bought it via a dealer. What options do I have now? Also, how can I confirm that the pins are undamaged?
You can only check the pins by opening the upper part of the [product_name], but that will void the warranty. I've attached a photo showing a card holder with bent pins.
I don’t think that’s the issue for two reasons: If the device is powered and I insert the SD card tray, it attempts to read it but fails to submit. So, I suspect the pins aren’t bent.

I've used many microSD cards from different brands and sizes, and never had any issues. The last worked was 64GB, which I partitioned to 32GB and formatted with FAT32. No problems there. If your [product_name] isn't working, it might be due to a faulty card or bent pins in the slot. I'm not aware of any other common problems.
Brand new card… looks like my luck ran out. If the dealer can’t help, what should I do now?
Also got a new error: Only FAT32 is supported. Please check the format of your card. Does that help?
Format the card using FAT32. What response are you expecting? New cards aren’t usually formatted this way by default.
It’s already formatted as FAT32. Anyway, thanks.
If your card is truly formatted in FAT32, you shouldn't see that error message.

Hello, Based on this, it seems the [product_name] or CPU isn’t reading the SD card correctly, so likely there's a hardware issue. I managed to remove the SD card tray without fully taking the controller apart—there’s a clip on the left side that lets you take it out, so I think my warranty is still valid. The pins seem nearly perfect—one is barely misaligned by 0.05mm, so that seems normal. It doesn’t match the bent-pin pictures. So, I suspect an internal issue with the CPU board, perhaps a broken power rail or just bad luck. I’ll see if my local distributor can assist, otherwise I have a pricey controller that’s unreliable. The LTE module also doesn’t meet all my needs, so I’m still searching for a proper solution.

Hi, Remove the microSD card and test. If the display remains blank, the [product_name] might be faulty—contact your dealer for an exchange. If it operates normally, try another card. Remember to format the card using a Windows PC, since FAT32 drivers on Mac or Linux may use different settings. Hope this helps.
Hello all, I contacted the dealer who is willing to exchange the device. Hoping it works out. Thanks for your support.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is experiencing issues with their new [product_name], where the device fails to respond when a properly formatted SD card is inserted and powered on. The display remains inactive until the card is removed, and the card isn't detected during operation. Forum members suggest potential compatibility problems, possible bent pins in the card slot, and very strict FAT32 formatting requirements, which complicate troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects their [product_name] to reliably detect and work with a standard FAT32 SD card without causing the system to become unresponsive after power cycling. They also seek straightforward guidance and support for troubleshooting or replacing defective hardware.
